examples.question_text:
A machine produces packets with mean mass $42.6$ g and standard deviation $3.5$ g.
(a) Calculate the $z$-score for a packet of mass $48.8$ g.
(b) Calculate the $z$-score for a packet of mass $38.1$ g.
Give the $z$-scores correct to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
Write $z=\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$.
(a) $\begin{aligned}z&=\dfrac{48.8-42.6}{3.5}\\&=\dfrac{6.2}{3.5}\\&=1.771428\ldots\\&\approx1.8\end{aligned}$
The packet is above the mean, so its score is positive.
(b) $\begin{aligned}z&=\dfrac{38.1-42.6}{3.5}\\&=\dfrac{-4.5}{3.5}\\&=-1.285714\ldots\\&\approx-1.3\end{aligned}$
The packet is below the mean, so its score is negative.

examples.question_text:
A test has mean $57$ and standard deviation $8$.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc}\text{Student}&A&B&C&D\\\hline\text{Mark}&69&51&57&61\end{array}$
(a) Calculate each student's standardised score.
(b) Describe B's result in terms of the mean and standard deviation.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Use $z=\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$ for each mark.
A: $z=\dfrac{69-57}{8}=1.5$.
B: $z=\dfrac{51-57}{8}=-0.75$.
C: $z=\dfrac{57-57}{8}=0$.
D: $z=\dfrac{61-57}{8}=0.5$.
(b) B is $0.75$ standard deviations below the mean.
C's score of $0$ shows that the mark equals the mean, not that the mark is zero.

examples.question_text:
(a) The times (seconds) to solve a puzzle are $8,11,13,15,19$. Use a calculator to find the mean and population standard deviation, then calculate the $z$-score of the slowest time. Give the standard deviation and $z$-score correct to $1$ decimal place.
(b) Fun-run times have mean $18$ minutes $24$ seconds and standard deviation $1$ minute $40$ seconds. Calculate the $z$-score of a time of $16$ minutes $9$ seconds.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Enter all five times in statistics mode and read the population standard deviation.
$\mu=13.2$, $\sigma=3.709447\ldots\approx3.7$ seconds.
The slowest time is the largest, $x=19$.
Keep the unrounded standard deviation in the calculation.
$\begin{aligned}z&=\dfrac{19-13.2}{3.709447\ldots}\\&=1.563575\ldots\\&\approx1.6\end{aligned}$
(b) Use seconds throughout.
$\mu=18\times60+24=1104$, $\sigma=60+40=100$, $x=16\times60+9=969$.
$\begin{aligned}z&=\dfrac{969-1104}{100}\\&=\dfrac{-135}{100}\\&=-1.35\end{aligned}$
All three time quantities must use the same unit.

examples.question_text:
Write the $z$-score of a value that is:
(a) $1.7$ standard deviations above the mean
(b) $0.6$ standard deviations below the mean.
examples.solution_text:
A $z$-score counts standard deviations from the mean. Above is positive; below is negative.
(a) $z=1.7$.
(b) $z=-0.6$.
